children: Arabica coffee futures hit a 2-1/2-month low on Thursday, with exchange stocks edging away from a recent 27-year low, while sugar and cocoa prices also fell.
fell 0.7% to $2.7960 per lb by 1354 GMT after hitting a 2-1/2-month low of $2.7615.
* Dealers noted a modest rise in exchange stocks, although they remain far below year-earlier levels.
* Exchange stocks stood at 233,479 bags as of September 16, up from a 27-year low of 217,646 bags a day earlier. The bulk of the additional coffee (15,250 bags) came from Brazil.
* At the same time last year, stocks stood at 668,874 bags.
* Dealers said the market's recent weakness also reflected a favourable outlook for next year's crop in Brazil.
* Recent rains in top robusta producer Vietnam have the potential to be beneficial for coffee trees, a trader based in the country's coffee belt said.
lost 1.1% to 17.78 cents per lb after setting a two-week low of 17.58 cents.
* Dealers said lower crude oil prices contributed to the weakness in the sugar market, potentially leading to more use of cane in Brazil and India to make the sweetener rather than biofuel ethanol.
* Dealers said supplies remained ample with December trading at a discount of around £173 to March (LCC-1=R).
